counselling.name: MOE Education & Career Guidance (ECG) Counsellors
counselling.description: Every MOE secondary school, JC, polytechnic and ITE has trained ECG counsellors. They help students explore education options, career interests and subject choices. Free for all students.
counselling.how_to_access: Approach your school's ECG counsellor directly, or ask your form teacher to refer you.

counselling.name: MySkillsFuture ECG Portal
counselling.description: Online career interest profiling, education pathway explorer and ECG centre appointments. Students can book a 1-on-1 session with an ECG counsellor at an ECG centre.
counselling.how_to_access: Register at https://www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg and use the ECG portal, or book an appointment at an ECG centre.

counselling.name: CHAT (Community Health Assessment Team)
counselling.description: Free mental health screening and support for youth aged 16–30. Walk-in or online assessment. Referral to appropriate support if needed. Run by IMH.
counselling.how_to_access: Walk in to CHAT @ Orchard (8 Grange Road) or start online at chat.mentalhealth.sg

counselling.name: Singapore Association for Mental Health (SAMH)
counselling.description: Counselling, case management and community mental health services. Helpline available.
counselling.how_to_access: Helpline: 1800-283-7019 (Mon–Fri 9am–6pm). Referral via GP or self-referral.

counselling.name: Samaritans of Singapore (SOS)
counselling.description: 24-hour emotional support and crisis intervention for those in distress. Completely confidential.

counselling.name: TOUCH Youth Intervention
counselling.description: Individual and group counselling for at-risk youth. School-based student support, family services.
counselling.how_to_access: Via school referral or self-referral to TOUCH Community Services.

career_guidance.name: MOE ECG Centres
career_guidance.description: Free career guidance sessions with professional ECG counsellors. Help students match interests to education pathways and future careers. Located at multiple centres island-wide.
career_guidance.eligibility: Secondary school students, N/O/A-level students, poly/ITE students
career_guidance.how_to_access: Book via MySkillsFuture portal. Locations: Tampines, Queenstown, Woodlands.

career_guidance.name: MySkillsFuture for Students
career_guidance.description: Career interest profiler, skills explorer, education pathway mapping, job market insights. Personalised based on your profile. Free for all Singaporeans.
career_guidance.eligibility: Secondary school and above, Singapore Citizens and PRs

career_guidance.name: Workforce Singapore (WSG) Career Centres
career_guidance.description: Career coaching, resume writing, interview preparation, job matching. Especially useful for poly/ITE graduates entering the workforce or mid-career switches.
career_guidance.eligibility: Job seekers and career switchers in Singapore
career_guidance.how_to_access: Walk in or book appointment at WSG Career Centres (Aliwal Arts Centre, Kolam Ayer, etc.).

career_guidance.name: e2i (Employment and Employability Institute)
career_guidance.description: Career guidance, job matching and upgrading support under NTUC. Offers career fairs and industry networking events.
career_guidance.how_to_access: Walk in to e2i centres or visit e2i.com.sg

career_guidance.name: Polytechnic Career Services
career_guidance.description: Each polytechnic has a dedicated career services centre offering internship placement, job fairs, employer networking, and career counselling.
career_guidance.eligibility: Current students and recent graduates of respective polytechnic
career_guidance.how_to_access: Contact your polytechnic's Career Services / Student Development office.

career_guidance.name: ITE Career & Placement Services
career_guidance.description: ITE helps graduates find jobs through industry partnerships, job fairs and career coaching. Strong placement rates in technical sectors.
career_guidance.how_to_access: Contact your ITE college's career services unit.

talks_events.name: Polytechnic Open Houses
talks_events.description: Annual open houses where prospective students explore courses, facilities and talk to current students and lecturers. Usually held in October–November.

talks_events.name: ITE Open House
talks_events.description: Annual open house at all 3 ITE colleges. Showcases NITEC and Higher NITEC courses, workshops and employer partners.

talks_events.name: University Open Days & Information Sessions
talks_events.description: NUS, NTU, SMU, SUTD, SIT and SUSS hold open houses and information days. Great for A-level and poly students exploring degree options.

talks_events.name: MOE Secondary School Open Houses
talks_events.description: Secondary schools hold open houses in October–November for P6 students and parents. Opportunity to understand school culture, CCAs and academic programmes.

talks_events.name: National Youth Council (NYC) Programmes
talks_events.description: NYC runs youth leadership programmes, community service initiatives and career exposure events for youths aged 15–35.

talks_events.name: Career Fairs & Job Expos
talks_events.description: SGJobsFest, e2i Career Fairs and polytechnic/ITE career fairs connect graduating students with employers. Many have on-the-spot interviews.
talks_events.typical_timing: Year-round; major fairs in March–April and September

scholarships.name: Public Service Commission (PSC) Scholarships
scholarships.value: Full tuition + living allowance + return airfare (overseas)
scholarships.description: Prestigious scholarships to develop future leaders of Singapore's public service. Includes President's Scholarship (most prestigious), PSC Merit Scholarship, and various statutory board scholarships.
scholarships.eligibility: Outstanding A-level / IB / poly students. Singapore Citizens. Strong academics + leadership.

scholarships.name: SAF Scholarship (Singapore Armed Forces)
scholarships.description: Develops future SAF leaders. Covers all degree levels. Recipients commissioned as officers.
scholarships.eligibility: Singapore Citizens with strong A-level / IB results. Must complete NS first.

scholarships.name: MHA Scholarship (Ministry of Home Affairs)
scholarships.description: For future leaders in SPF (Police), SCDF (Civil Defence) or ICA. Includes mentorship and leadership development.
scholarships.eligibility: Singapore Citizens with strong academic record

scholarships.name: MOE Teaching Scholarship
scholarships.description: For those passionate about teaching. Leads to a teaching career in MOE schools. Local or overseas degree options.
scholarships.eligibility: A-level / IB / poly students with good results and passion for education

scholarships.name: A*STAR Scholarships (National Science Scholarship)
scholarships.value: Full tuition + generous stipend + research opportunities
scholarships.description: For students passionate about research and science. National Science Scholarship (NSS) for undergrad, Singapore International Graduate Award (SINGA) for PhD.
scholarships.eligibility: Strong STEM results, genuine research interest
scholarships.bond: Varies; research placement at A*STAR institutes

scholarships.name: MOE Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS)
scholarships.value: School fees waiver + free textbooks + uniforms + transport assistance
scholarships.description: For families with monthly household income ≤ $3,000 or per capita income ≤ $750. Covers primary school through JC/poly/ITE.
scholarships.eligibility: Singapore Citizens in government / government-aided schools. Income criteria apply.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Apply through your child's school at the start of the year.

scholarships.name: Yayasan MENDAKI Bursaries
scholarships.description: Financial assistance for Malay/Muslim students from lower-income families at all education levels.
scholarships.eligibility: Malay/Muslim Singapore Citizens. Income criteria apply.

scholarships.name: CDAC Bursaries (Chinese Development Assistance Council)
scholarships.description: Financial assistance for Chinese students from lower-income families.
scholarships.eligibility: Chinese Singapore Citizens/PRs. Income criteria apply.

scholarships.name: SINDA Bursaries (Singapore Indian Development Association)
scholarships.description: Financial assistance and academic support for Indian students.
scholarships.eligibility: Indian Singapore Citizens/PRs. Income criteria apply.

scholarships.name: NUS Scholarships (Merit & Need-based)
scholarships.value: Full to partial tuition; NUS Merit Scholarship covers full fees
scholarships.description: NUS offers merit scholarships (top students) and need-based bursaries. Includes Global Merit Scholarship for most outstanding students.
scholarships.eligibility: Admitted NUS students. Merit: exceptional results. Need: household income criteria.

scholarships.name: SkillsFuture Credit
scholarships.description: Every Singapore Citizen aged 25+ receives SkillsFuture Credit for approved courses at universities, polytechnics, ITE and private providers. Use for part-time degrees, professional certs, short courses.

earn_and_learn.name: ITE Work-Study Programme (WSP)
earn_and_learn.description: Alternating blocks of school-based learning and company-based training. Students are paid a monthly allowance by the company. Leads to Higher NITEC qualification with industry experience.
earn_and_learn.eligibility: ITE students in selected courses. Must be offered by participating companies.
earn_and_learn.allowance: Monthly training allowance paid by employer (varies by industry)

earn_and_learn.name: Polytechnic Work-Study Diploma (WSDip)
earn_and_learn.description: Structured programme combining poly study with structured on-the-job training at a company. Same diploma as full-time study but with paid work experience built in.
earn_and_learn.eligibility: Selected poly students; companies and poly must have WSDip arrangement
earn_and_learn.allowance: Paid by company during work attachment periods

earn_and_learn.name: SkillsFuture Earn & Learn Programme
earn_and_learn.description: Fresh poly diploma or ITE Higher NITEC graduates are hired by a company and sponsored to pursue a part-time degree or specialist diploma while working. Company pays salary. Government provides training grant to company.
earn_and_learn.eligibility: Fresh poly diploma holders (within 2 years of graduation). Singapore Citizens and PRs.

earn_and_learn.name: Professional Conversion Programmes (PCP)
earn_and_learn.description: Structured training programmes to help professionals switch to a new career sector. Employer hires candidate, government co-funds salary during training period.
earn_and_learn.eligibility: Singapore Citizens and PRs. Varies by programme — some for fresh grads, others for mid-career.
earn_and_learn.salary_support: Up to 90% of salary supported for eligible candidates during training period

earn_and_learn.name: NTU / NUS Industry Attachment & Co-op Programmes
earn_and_learn.description: Structured industry attachments (6–12 months) or co-op programmes where students work in real companies. Paid. Many lead to job offers. NUS iCPEX, NTU Industry Attachment.
earn_and_learn.eligibility: NUS / NTU students in eligible programmes

earn_and_learn.name: SGUnited Traineeships / Apprenticeships
earn_and_learn.description: Government-supported traineeship programme connecting fresh graduates with host companies for structured on-the-job training. Monthly stipend paid. Builds industry-ready skills.
earn_and_learn.eligibility: Fresh graduates (ITE, poly, university). Singapore Citizens and PRs.
earn_and_learn.stipend: Varies by qualification: ITE ~$1,200/month, Poly ~$1,500/month, Degree ~$1,800/month
